articles.title: Comitê Paralímpico oferece cursos gratuitos de formação esportiva em SP; veja como participar | G1
articles.standfirst: Formações presenciais e on-line são voltadas a professores de Educação Física, treinadores, árbitros e outros profissionais interessados em atuar com pessoas com deficiência.
articles.summary: Formações presenciais e on-line são voltadas a professores de Educação Física, treinadores, árbitros e outros profissionais interessados em atuar com pessoas com deficiência.
articles.body:
Partida entre Agafuc e Corinthians pelo Campeonato Brasileiro de Futebol de Cegos, realizada no Centro de Treinamento Paralímpico, em São Paulo, em 23 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: Alessandra Cabral/CPB

O Comitê Paralímpico Brasileiro (CPB) oferece cursos gratuitos de formação e qualificação em esporte paralímpico no estado de São Paulo. As capacitações são voltadas a professores de Educação Física, treinadores, árbitros e outros profissionais que atuam ou desejam trabalhar com pessoas com deficiência.

Com cursos presenciais e pela internet, as formações abordam diferentes modalidades esportivas, além de temas como inclusão e classificação de atletas. Os interessados podem consultar as opções disponíveis e fazer a inscrição pela plataforma Educação Paralímpica.

Desde 2017, o programa registrou mais de 31 mil conclusões de cursos em São Paulo. Segundo o CPB, foram realizados 285 cursos presenciais no estado, com a participação de 7.927 alunos. A plataforma também reúne 19.305 usuários cadastrados em território paulista.

Em todo o Brasil, são cerca de 93 mil usuários cadastrados.

As capacitações abrangem modalidades como atletismo, natação, badminton, basquete em cadeira de rodas, bocha, canoagem, futebol de cegos, goalball, halterofilismo, paraesgrima, tiro com arco e vôlei sentado.

Também há conteúdos sobre classificação esportiva e Educação Física para estudantes com síndrome de Down e Transtorno do Espectro Autista (TEA).

Na parte teórica, uma das opções é o curso "Movimento Paralímpico: Fundamentos Básicos do Esporte", que aborda a história do esporte paralímpico, os tipos de deficiência elegíveis para competições e as estratégias de ensino de modalidades adaptadas. A

formação é pré-requisito para diversas outras capacitações oferecidas pelo programa.

Os cursos podem ser presenciais, on-line ou híbridos. No ensino a distância, há opções com aulas ao vivo e outras em que o participante pode acompanhar o conteúdo conforme sua disponibilidade.

Quem se interessar pela capacitação tanto online quanto presencial deve acessar o site da instituição, consultar as formações disponíveis e verificar os requisitos para cada curso. (Clique aqui para acessar a plataforma).

As inscrições e a disponibilidade de vagas variam de acordo com a capacitação e novas turmas são divulgadas semanalmente no site do CPB.

articles.title: BBC Sport quiz: Who am I? Guess WSL footballer No 11
articles.summary: Work out the identity of today's player in as few attempts as possible.
articles.body:
The rules are simple. Each Sunday there's a new Women' Super League footballer and the challenge is to guess who they are in as few attempts as possible.

After each wrong guess you unlock a new clue. The fewer clues you need to get the right answer, the more points you score.

Three is a good score, four or five points is exceptional.

So take part and return for more tomorrow.

Today's player and clues set by BBC Sport's Adam Millington.

articles.title: Cubarsí tiene una espina clavada contra el Atlético
articles.standfirst: El curso pasado, dos acciones suyas fueron claves en las eliminatorias de Copa y Champions
articles.summary: El curso pasado, dos acciones suyas fueron claves en las eliminatorias de Copa y Champions
articles.body: Cubarsí afronta esta noche una cita especial en el Metropolitano. El defensa catalán tiene una cuenta pendiente con el Atlético de Madrid después de lo sucedido la temporada pasada en dos de los enfrentamientos entre ambos equipos. Dos acciones protagonizadas por el central azulgrana marcaron, en mayor o menor medida, el desenlace de las eliminatorias de Copa y de Champions. Ahora, el catalán tiene una oportunidad para quitarse una espina que todavía tiene clavada. El primero de esos momentos llegó en febrero, durante la vuelta de las semifinales de la Copa. Con un contundente 4-0 en el marcador, Cubarsí logró marcar en el minuto 52 un gol que podía alimentar las esperanzas de remontada del conjunto azulgrana. Sin embargo, la alegría duró poco. El tanto fue anulado por fuera de juego y la polémica llegó porque la revisión del VAR se prolongó durante seis minutos debido a un problema técnico en el sistema. Los colegiados tuvieron que trazar manualmente las líneas para determinar la posición del defensor. En la vuelta, el Barcelona logró imponerse por 3-0, un resultado fue insuficiente para alcanzar la final, pero en el recuerdo quedó aquella acción de Cubarsí y la sensación de que el gol anulado pudo haber dado otro rumbo a la eliminatoria. El segundo episodio tuvo lugar en la ida de los cuartos de final de la Champions. En aquella ocasión, el protagonismo de Cubarsí llegó por una acción defensiva sobre Giuliano que terminó con su expulsión. El catalán derribó al atacante rojiblanco cuando este se disponía a encarar la portería y era el último defensor azulgrana. Una intervención que condicionó por completo el encuentro. La jugada se produjo en el minuto 43. En un primer momento, el colegiado mostró tarjeta amarilla al central, pero desde la sala del VAR le advirtieron de que debía revisar la acción. Después de ir al monitor, el árbitro modificó su decisión y mostró la tarjeta roja directa a Cubarsí. La expulsión dejó al conjunto azulgrana con diez y, además, esa acción dio paso al posterior tanto de Julián Álvarez. El encuentro terminó con un 0-2. Las consecuencias de aquella acción fueron más allá. La expulsión impidió que Cubarsí pudiera participar en el partido de vuelta, en el Metropolitano, donde el Barça fue eliminado de la competición europea. Por ello, el compromiso de esta noche tiene un significado especial para el defensa que, además, en las próximas horas puede ser designado como Golden Boy por su excelente rendimiento. Más allá de los tres puntos, Cubarsí tiene ante sí la oportunidad de cerrar una cuenta pendiente con el Atlético.

images.caption: Cubarsí, en el cruce contra el Atlético de la temporada pasada. FRANCESC ADELANTADO

articles.title: Misery Index: Matt Rhule is running out of answers as another Nebraska season spirals out of control
articles.summary: Though Nebraska fans have dealt with many losing streaks over the last couple decades, this one may be hitting them a bit differently. But they aren't alone...
articles.body:
The Nebraska job is getting to Matt Rhule. A week ago, he started his press conference with a 20-minute soliloquy/opening statement that felt like a therapy session. He spends ridiculous amounts of time arguing with the referees. Now, after firing Dana Holgorsen on Saturday , he'll soon be on his third offensive coordinator in four seasons.

But it's hard to tell who's going off the deep end quicker in this relationship — the head coach or a fan base that is finding new ways to be aghast at their program, which has gone from 5-0 to 5-4 and failed to crack 20 points in any of those losses.

The latest indignity, the one that demanded Rhule sacrifice a staff member, was a 24-13 loss to Illinois . But in firing Holgorsen, Rhule tacitly admitted how screwed up his whole process has been from the time he's gotten to Lincoln.

Holgorsen, who came from the Mike Leach offensive tree at Texas Tech, was never going to be a great fit in the Big Ten. Rhule hired him anyway. He was also going to be a square peg in a round hole building an offense around Dylan Raiola, a quarterback with limited mobility. Rhule hired him anyway. Then when Raiola transferred to Oregon, they rebuilt it around Anthony Colandrea, who has a lot of running ability. A little more than a week ago, Nebraska announced that Colandrea had signed to return to Nebraska for a fifth year in 2027. Then they turned around and fired Holgorsen, ostensibly meaning Rhule's next offensive coordinator hire will once again have to fit around a quarterback rather than the other way around.

Though Nebraska fans have dealt with many losing streaks over the last couple decades, this one is hitting them differently. (In retrospect, the Bo Pelini era looks pretty good, eh?) And what makes it different is Rhule's contract.

After Penn State fired James Franklin a year ago, Nebraska chose to extend Rhule through 2032, saddling the school with a buyout in the $60 million range. Because of Rhule's close relationship with Penn State athletic director Pat Kraft (they worked together at Temple) and ties to the school (Rhule went to high school in State College and played at Penn State), he was going to be their No. 1 choice. Nebraska felt at the time the program was on the right track and didn't want to go into coach search mode so they made the long-term investment to keep him.

It now looks like the wrong decision, but that's in the past. The question is what Nebraska can do to now to either triage the situation or extricate the school from it.

Fans are mad at everyone, and they're going to be very loud about it the rest of this season. They could potentially even end the school's famous sellout streak going back to 1962, which has long been a point of pride for the Cornhuskers.

After what he did at Temple and Baylor, Rhule looked like a can't-miss hire moving up to a program with Nebraska's resources. But like the five Nebraska coaches before him, Rhule hasn't been able to figure out the place or get the breakthrough win that would calm everyone down.

Instead, the pressure goes up week by week, and Rhule wears it poorly, without articulating a plan to get things fixed. It's hard to see how any of this gets better this season. And if Rhule is back in 2027 because the contract is simply too prohibitive, the school should prepare for an onslaught of unhappiness from its fan base.

Until then, Rhule is just going to continue stressing himself and everybody else in Nebraska out, making the Huskers the most miserable fan base in America in Week 10.

ACC: Let's talk about NC State. The Wolfpack lost to Duke, 41-3, which does not move the needle much at this point given Dave Doeren's firing a couple weeks ago. NC State fans are either still celebrating that he's done or have completely moved on to basketball season. But at some point in the next several days, it's practically a lock that NC State will hire Philip Rivers as head coach. Rivers, 44, is an NC State legend and an eight-time Pro Bowler in the NFL. He also has no coaching experience other than at a private high school in Alabama. NC State fans should equally be excited about the potential of this marriage and terrified of the track record. Lots of schools have tried hiring coaches who didn't have the experience necessary to run a college football program. None of them have really worked, including the most recent example of Trent Dilfer getting fired after going 9-21 at UAB. NC State is going to do this because some influential donors feel it in their hearts, and because it's probably less costly than hiring someone else and because athletic director Boo Corrigan doesn't really have enough juice there to squash it. NC State is one of those places that has always been in the "sleeping giant" category, but Rivers isn't a sleeping-giant hire. It's the kind of hire you make when you don't feel very confident about the kind of coach you can attract on the open market and are going to make a big bet on star power. Maybe it will work and maybe it won't, but the odds are against it and NC State fans should go into this with eyes wide open that it might be a disaster.

Big 12: Collin Klein was the perfect hire on paper to lead Kansas State back to contention in this league. He played quarterback there under Bill Snyder, spent seven years on staff, including a couple as offensive coordinator, then went to Texas A&M where he called plays for a team that made the College Football Playoff a year ago. But at least in his first season he's given fans some reasons to be concerned about his readiness for the big chair. At 1-5 in the Big 12, Kansas State is down at the bottom with Colorado and Kansas, which is not where this program has grown accustomed to being. But without great recruiting geography or resources, Kansas State's secret has always been mostly about the coaching, from Snyder working miracles to the underrated Chris Klieman never finishing worse than 4-5 in the conference. Going from coordinator to head coach is a big adjustment, and maybe it's simply going to take Klein some time to find his footing. But if he's not eventually giving Kansas State an edge in the coaching chair, it'll be tough to get back to even the Klieman level of winning consistently.

SEC: The thing Florida fans will appreciate most about Jon Sumrall is that he sounds like one of them in his passion for the game and how much it bothers him when the team doesn't perform well. He owns it, doesn't make excuses and says all the things fans want to hear after they've just gotten their guts ripped out. At the same time, many Gators fans were skeptical of hiring another coach from the Group of Six level (Sumrall came from Tulane) and have seen this season completely spiral on them the last couple weeks, most recently with a 23-7 loss to Oklahoma. At 5-4, Florida isn't really overachieving or underachieving what was expected, but the way the season has played out is frustrating. After such a hot start, including wins over Auburn, Ole Miss and Texas, the Gators have also been blown out by Missouri and South Carolina, weren't competitive at all against Georgia and now gained just 203 yards of offense with two turnovers at home against Oklahoma. Afterward, Sumrall talk about how ticked off he is, which is fine. But the adjustment he's going to have to make is getting SEC-level players to feel that as well when they're all getting paid a lot of money. It's one thing to imbue that attitude into your team at Troy or Tulane, where he coached previously, but something might be getting lost in the translation.

Group of Six: It's never a good sign when an athletic director has to issue a statement of apology hours after a game because of an apocalyptically bad result. But after a 60-10 loss at home to Tulsa, that's exactly what Tulane's David Harris did, calling the performance "unacceptable" and "particularly alarming." What the statement doesn't do, however, is point to any imminent change at the program level, which may make some fans madder than if Harris had said nothing at all. Because if Tulane was going to fire Will Hall right away, it would have done so instead of releasing a statement that ultimately amounts to a whole bunch of nothing. The issue for Harris, who hired Hall despite a 14-30 record at Southern Miss from 2021-24, is that he will have to convince donors to step up and rectify a bad decision. So far, at least, it seems Tulane might have some issues figuring that part out.

Ryan Day: Even though Ohio State was disappointed by losing in the CFP quarterfinals a year ago, the entire season was a bit of a victory lap where Day could finally open up about how winning a national title had removed a huge burden from his life. This year, he's learning how quickly that "get out of jail free" card expires at a place like Ohio State. It would be unfair to say Day is back on the hot seat after a 41-28 loss to Oregon because there's no evidence it's true. But it's not necessarily untrue either. When you're the Buckeyes coach, the championship glow burns out quicker than a birthday candle, and the demand to at least be in that mix again and again never relents. Ohio State is probably not going to make the playoff this year, but the hard part about evaluating its 6-3 record is that it has lost two straight games with a freshman backup quarterback who probably isn't ready to lead a team to playoff glory. At the same time, why would the Buckeyes' defense completely collapse as a result? Yes, every part of a football team is connected, and the timing of losing quarterback Julian Sayin to injury right before playing USC and Oregon couldn't have been worse. Still, the nature of those defeats gives the impression that something is off in Columbus, and the atmosphere could get even spicier than it was before Day's national title breakthrough.

Pete Golding: In retrospect, this was a pretty tough situation at Ole Miss for Golding to manage. Last year, it was pure honeymoon after Lane Kiffin walked away from Ole Miss to take the LSU job, leaving Golding to soak up all the glory from a CFP semifinal run without any of the scrutiny. But in the long-term reality portion of the marriage, Golding is now in front of a fan base whose expectations were raised by the Kiffin era. And losing 42-7 to Georgia is the kind of result that feels like the more traditional version of Ole Miss fans had forgotten about the last several years. With their third loss, the Rebels are pretty much eliminated from CFP contention, and that's going to seem like a big missed opportunity when you convinced two of the most dynamic offensive players in America in Trinidad Chambliss and Kewan Lacy to come back and play a full season for Golding. At the same time, a lot of folks underrated the possibility that Ole Miss wasn't going to be as good as a year ago due to the players Kiffin took with him to LSU. There also needs to be a discussion about why the Ole Miss defense has regressed so badly from the last couple years when Golding was focusing exclusively on that side of the ball.

Barry Odom: Nobody is going to feel sorry for a coach whose worst-case scenario is coaching at a school for a few years, losing a bunch of games and walking away with nearly $30 million. But we see coaches all the time in college who are so eager to move up the ladder that they end up taking the wrong job. Why did Odom go to Purdue in the first place? It would be a fair question to ask himself after a 34-29 loss to Maryland at home, which is all kinds of bad on every conceivable level. Odom is now 5-16 as he nears the end of his second season at Purdue with just two Big Ten wins. When your program is in that state, you can't blow the kind of opportunity the Boilermakers had this week, facing a bad Maryland team that has already fired Mike Locksley and had lost 13 conference games in a row. Purdue has shown some signs of improvement this year, but losing to the Terps is just a season-killer and a reminder how tough it is to sustain momentum when you're trying to claw out of such a deep hole. Odom, who was fired in 2019 after four seasons at Missouri, had to drop down to the Mountain West to rebuild his career and did such a good job at UNLV, going 19-8 in two seasons there, that he became a power conference candidate again. In retrospect, it might have been a better move to hold on for one more season in Las Vegas and return to a place where you're not constantly pushing a boulder uphill.

James Franklin: No coach in the history of college football has done more lobbying for small university towns to improve their aviation infrastructure for the benefit of football teams. At Penn State, Franklin famously complained about having to bus 90 minutes to Harrisburg for a trip to the West Coast because the runway wasn't long enough in State College to accommodate a plane with that much fuel. Now at Virginia Tech, Franklin is once again in a town where flying in and out isn't easy, with most commercial traffic going to Roanoke about 40 miles away. Asked this week about in-state recruiting, Franklin's mind immediately went to … the airport situation. "We also have to go nationally," he said. "That's where having an airport right on campus is going to be important. We're going to be very aggressive in doing that." At this point, Franklin is like Paul McCartney playing "Hey Jude" and "Let it Be." The set list is always going to include one or two of his greatest hits. Franklin, however, will need to do a lot better than a 51-28 loss to SMU before they build him an airport.

Holy War heartbreak: BYU's second-half drive chart in a 28-20 loss at Utah reads like a football death sentence. Interception, punt, punt, interception, interception. "If you know anything about this rivalry, that is not the way to win it," BYU coach Kalani Sitake said. Unless BYU can get really lucky and find a way into the Big 12 championship game, the Cougars' playoff hopes are going to endure a really nervous few weeks. Yeah, the win over Notre Dame will help, but is 10-2 good enough without a conference championship? Meanwhile, BYU fans may have to watch their rivals reach the CFP before they do, which causes all kinds of uncomfortable dinner conversations in a state where allegiances are split down the middle. Then again, it was right there for BYU this time. Among quarterback Bear Bachmeier's four interceptions was an unfortunate mistake in the end zone when the Cougars had third-and-goal at the 2-yard line. If Bachmeier makes that play, the entire course of the season, the playoff chase and the Beehive State rivalry might be different.

Frog follies: TCU's season has been one long fourth-quarter nightmare. Even at 4-5, the combined margin of defeat is 25 points. Their most lopsided loss of the year was 21-13 at UCF. When you're right there in every single game but lose more than you win, no moment feels safe. And so it was with 1:45 remaining at Arizona, when the Wildcats scored a touchdown but missed a 2-point conversion that would have tied it. At TCU this season, that's still plenty of time for something to go wrong. Right on cue, disaster struck when Arizona went to the pooch kickoff and TCU's Ed Small let it fall through his breadbasket. When Arizona recovered at the TCU 26, it was already in field goal range. It got a little closer and delivered a dagger to win 29-28 and ratchet up the talk that TCU may run off Sonny Dykes at some point in the near future.

Tiger trouble: After Missouri's 34-20 loss to Texas, head coach Eli Drinkwitz tried to do the thing where he wanted everyone to know he thought the officiating was terrible but didn't want to say it directly so that he wouldn't get in trouble with the SEC office. "If I say what I want to say, I'm going to get fined until I don't have any retirement, and I'm not gonna do that," he said. "I'm not gonna blame the officials. That would be disrespectful to Coach [Steve] Sarkisian and his team." You can't blame a man for wanting to hold onto his money, but Missouri fans would have appreciated a good, old-fashioned officiating rant even if it would have cost Drinkwitz a little bit of the $10 million a year he makes. Because from a Missouri perspective, it sure seemed like the big video replays and close calls almost all went against them, including a bizarre fumble by Texas quarterback Arch Manning late in the third quarter that looked like an incompletion but actually turned into a 12-yard gain for the Longhorns.

Was it a bad call or just bad luck? It's hard to tell whether linebacker Brian Huff knocked the ball from Manning's hand or whether he had already started his throwing motion, but the call went Texas' way at a key moment. An incompletion would have made it fourth down with Texas trailing by seven. Instead, they scored to tie the game and dominated from there.

articles.body: El Elche, el peor local de LaLiga, recibe al Real Betis en el Martínez Valero en un partido correspondiente a la jornada 12 de LaLiga EA Sports. Los de Anselmi buscan su primer triunfo en casa, mientras que los de Pellegrini quieren olvidar la derrota sufrida en Dortmund en Champions. Alvaro Valles y Marc Roca, que apuntan a titulares, son dos de los grandes protagonistas en la previa del partido tras la llamada de Luis de la Fuente. El Elche ha mejorado, pero le falta ganar un partido delante de su afición. El partido entre Elche y Real Betis de la jornada 12 de LaLiga EA Sports se juega el sábado 8 de noviembre a las 14:00 horas. El partido entre Elche y Real Betis de la jornada 12 de LaLiga EA Sports se podrá ver por televisión en directo a través de DAZN. También se podrá seguir el partido a través de la narración de Radio MARCA y con los comentarios en directo de MARCA.com. Desde dos horas antes, sigue la previa y los onces. Tras el encuentro, podrás leer la crónica, las declaraciones de los protagonistas y ver el resumen con las mejores jugadas y los goles.

articles.title: Lens predicted XI v Marseille: Ismaelo Ganiou and Franjo Ivanovic out
articles.summary: RC Lens are without the likes of Ismaelo Ganiou and Franjo Ivanovic as they prepare to host Olympique de Marseille on Sunday night.Les Sang et Or will look t...
articles.body:
RC Lens are without the likes of Ismaelo Ganiou and Franjo Ivanovic as they prepare to host Olympique de Marseille on Sunday night.

Les Sang et Or will look to bounce back from the midweek humiliation of a 9-1 defeat to Como 1907 on Wednesday. That defeat was the heaviest in the history of the UEFA Champions League and the heaviest home defeat in the competition's history.

If Lens are to bounce back, they must do so without a recognised centre-forward. Due to the concussion protocol, Ivanovic is ruled out. He joins the two other recognised centre-forwards, Odsonne Édouard and Abdallah Sima, on the sidelines. Florian Thauvin may lead the line in their absence. In defence, Ganiou and Maik Nawrocki are also out.

Robin Risser; Jean-Clair Todibo, Samson Baidoo, Jonathan Gradit; Matthieu Udol, Amadou Haidara, Yacine Titraoui, Ruben Aguilar; Florian Sotoca, Florian Thauvin, Mezian Mesloub. (L'Éq)

articles.title: Notre Dame’s Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa breaks ‘The U’ after sacking Darian Mensah
articles.summary: There are multiple developments coming out of Notre Dame’s 31-24 home victory over No. 1 Miami on Saturday night. The Fighting Irish are a genuine national t...
articles.body:
There are multiple developments coming out of Notre Dame's 31-24 home victory over No. 1 Miami on Saturday night. The Fighting Irish are a genuine national title contender now ensconced in the College Football Playoff, and quarterback CJ Carr secured his spot in the Heisman Trophy ceremony after completing 72.5 percent of his passes for 319 yards and three touchdowns. But fans cannot overlook another consequence of this signature win in South Bend .

Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa just formally established himself as one of the most impactful linebackers in the country. One specific moment best accentuated his game-changing performance. Less than a minute into the third quarter, and with his team leading 17-3, the 20-year-old American Samoan reinforced Notre Dame's momentum by recording a huge sack on Miami star QB Darian Mensah. This third-and-7 stop kept the Hurricanes on their back.

Actually, according to Viliamu-Asa, it broke their back. The 6-foot-3, 234-pound junior used his hands to form "The U" symbol before pretending to break it over his knee . This game meant a lot to him, especially given his recent thumb injury, but it also meant the world to the program.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The CFP selection committee essentially told the Fighting Irish that they would need to beat Miami in order to have a realistic shot at making the final 12-team bracket. Pressure was rising, and even though electric Canes wide receiver Malachi Toney was sidelined with an ankle injury, Notre Dame could have still tripped on the big stage. It certainly has before.

Not on this night, though. Despite allowing Miami to cut the deficit to one possession, Marcus Freeman's squad answered the committee's challenge. CJ Carr, WR Micah Gilbert (nine receptions for 98 yards and two touchdowns) and safety Luke Talich (clutch interception around midfield late in the third) all produced highlight-reel plays that will have a lasting impression on fans. But so too will the Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa sack.

And the ensuing celebration. The Fighting Irish (8-1) will have to prove themselves all over again in the CFP, as will the other competitors, but they aced the eye and result tests on Saturday. What more will be asked of Notre Dame football ? Fans will find out when the newest rankings are unveiled on Tuesday.

articles.title: Sanford, Houston hold off Cincinnati, 31-24, to remain perfect at home
articles.summary: Re’Shaun Sanford II’s breakaway run and career-high performance allow the Cougars to survive an upset-hungry Bearcats.
articles.body:
Although the warm Southeast Texas temperatures remained unseasonably warm, the November air flowed through TDECU Stadium as Houston opened the pivotal final month of a the regular season.

The Cougars entered Saturday ranked No. 17 by the College Football Playoff committee, firmly in contention for a berth in the 12-team field. But Cincinnati had already been a disruptor to playoff résumés this season, two weeks removed from knocking off an undefeated Texas Tech team. The Bearcats, however, arrived in Houston burdened by a 10-game losing streak in the all-important month of November.

The all-time series between the programs was deadlocked at 15-15, and fittingly, Saturday's installment came down to the wire. Houston never trailed, withstood a late Cincinnati comeback, and pulled away in the closing minutes for a 31-24 victory, improving to 5-0 at home this season.

"Last year we went 3-3 at home and we were undefeated on the road," Houston running back Re'Shaun Sanford II said. "We made it an emphasis: when people come to your house, you're supposed to defend it. It's a mentality thing. For us to be undefeated so far in this season, it speaks volumes to our maturity and the way we approach it as well."

Cincinnati knotted the score at 24-24 with 6:21 remaining, storming back from an early 14-0 deficit. However, Houston ensured the game would not be in balance for long. Exactly 71 seconds later, Sanford delivered the defining moment of the evening. The running back found a crease, juked a Bearcat defender out of his shoes, and sprinted 51 yards into the red paint of the end zone for the go-ahead touchdown.

"I had a couple that I wanted back in the first half where I could have just beat the last guy, but unfortunately, that didn't happen," Sanford said. "But the o-line and wide receivers did a good job of getting me to the third level, so I knew it was gonna come eventually. It was just the next play mentality. Keep churning away at the small runs and then break through. I knew it was gonna come."

Sanford reset his career-high with 126 rushing yards, marking the highest single-game rushing total by any Houston player this season. The ground attack also received a boost from Makhi Hughes, who complemented Sanford's explosiveness by churning out 90 yards on 12 carries.

"When people see Makhi, they see the bigger back — the hard-nosed, run-you-over type guy," Sanford said. "But over the course of the season, he's been working on his sauce. We go to work after practice every day and work on juke moves. Then he teaches me stuff like pass pro(tection) and really lowering my shoulder. It's almost the sense that we're the same player in a different body. We're really starting to teach each other our own traits that make us good and we've really been helping each other be better for one another."

After Sanford restored Houston's 7-point advantage, the defense put the finishing touches on the victory with an unusual game-sealing takeaway. In fact, the play initially went unnoticed by several players on the field.

With 2:11 remaining, Cincinnati quarterback JC French IV attempted to swing a screen pass to running back Zylan Perry. The pass was initially ruled incomplete, but Houston inside linebacker Christian Brathwaite recognized an opportunity and scooped up the loose ball. Following an official review, French's screen was determined to be a backward lateral, and Brathwaite was credited with the recovery. Houston's offense then ran out the remaining clock to secure the victory.

"It was just us locking in," Houston defensive tackle Quindario Lee said. "We had a few plays down the stretch where we didn't play good and gave up a few points. So we just had to lock in as a defense, come up with a few corrections, go out there and make that play."

Houston needed late-game heroics to eke out a one-score victory, but in the early moments after the opening kickoff, it appeared as if the Cougars were destined for a comfortable win. Houston constructed a 14-0 lead in under nine minutes of action with Conner Weigman delivering two touchdown strikes to Amare Thomas. The reigning First Team All-Big 12 receiver finished with six receptions for a game-high 78 receiving yards, accounting for 69 of his receiving yards after the catch.

"He's a lot bigger than you'd think. He's like 205 pounds and he's got great speed," Houston head coach Willie Fritz said of Thomas. "I had one of my friends say, 'What is he, about 190?' No, he's a bigger guy. He runs with power and knows when to do a good job of triangulating the ball. He had that happen one time when there were four guys trying to strip him. He's really good at the yards after a catch, which is huge. Some guys catch it, they catch it at 12 and get 12. He can catch it at 12 and get 16."

Cincinnati's offense overcame a three-and-out on its opening series and found a sustainable rhythm, with French orchestrating the comeback. The senior quarterback delivered two touchdown passes and ran in another from the goal line to flip that 14-0 deficit into a 24-24 tie.

The scoreboard wasn't the only adversity the Bearcats were required to overcome. They had several personnel setbacks, entering without starting center Taran Tyo. The offense's health situation only worsened when losing star running back Cole Tabb and leading wide receiver JV Gibson to in-game injuries. Despite the attrition, Cincinnati continued moving the ball effectively until the late turnover.

"We didn't get off to a great start, down 14 tonight," Cincinnati head coach Scott Satterfield said. "Our guys continued to fight, loved the fight in them. They came back and battled and ultimately tied the game up there on an unbelievable drive. I think we started our drive maybe on the (4-yard line). 96-yard drive, 16 plays. I mean it was like the whole fourth quarter. It was an incredible drive to put ourselves back in position there to tie the game here on the road against a really good Houston team. Unfortunately we gave the touchdown back up."

Two troubling streaks continued for Cincinnati in the hard-fought loss. The Bearcats (5-4, 2-4 Big 12) suffered their 11th consecutive November defeat and remained winless on the road this season at 0-3. They'll get a third opportunity to solidify bowl eligibility next Saturday at Iowa State, with a chance to snap both streaks simultaneously.

Meanwhile, the Cougars (7-2, 4-2 Big 12) kept their College Football Playoff aspirations alive if they can navigate the waters of November. Upcoming matchups against Colorado, West Virginia, and Baylor will determine whether Houston can capitalize on the opportunity it created for itself. After allowing Cincinnati to come back from an early deficit, the Cougars know the key to achieving their goals starts with stronger finishes to second halves.

"That's our main goal these last three games is to push and be a second half team," Lee said. "We gave up 51 points in the first half of this season and 117 on the back end. So we just gotta be that first and second half team. We just gotta push through."

articles.title: Hansi Flick faces two big decisions ahead of Atletico Madrid vs Barcelona clash
articles.summary: Barcelona will be aiming to maintain their lead at the top of the league table as they take on Atletico Madrid at the Metropolitano this evening.It has been...
articles.body:
Barcelona will be aiming to maintain their lead at the top of the league table as they take on Atletico Madrid at the Metropolitano this evening.

It has been a rough few weeks for the Catalans, who have suffered a few damning defeats while the injury crisis has worked, with Rodri becoming the latest player to pick up a knock.

However, it is not all bad news for Hansi Flick heading into this game, as he has been boosted by the return of both Eric Garcia and Andreas Christensen.

According to Diario SPORT , Flick faces a selection dilemma in two key areas, as Barcelona prepare to face Atleti at the Metropolitano this evening.

Eric Garcia can start vs Atletico Madrid. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images)

The report suggests that Garcia has recovered from his injury well before expected and is one of the starting candidates for Barcelona against Atletico Madrid.

Garcia could be a handy asset to have for Barça, especially with both Xavi Espart and Jules Kounde not available for this game due to injury.

The former Man City star, therefore, can operate in the right-back position and offer some defensive solidity which Barcelona have lacked lately.

Alternatively, Flick could choose not to risk the defender's fitness and continue with Brian Farinas, who has done well in the past couple of matches.

De Jong could appear as a Rodri replacement. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Rodri is out for the time being with a fresh injury , which raises the question: Who will be his replacement against Atletico Madrid this evening.

Flick has to choose between either Frenkie de Jong or Marc Bernal. De Jong seems like the obvious pick given that the Dutchman is finally back to full fitness.

However, de Jong hasn't had too much action this season and could be lacking that bit of edge against an Atleti side, who can overwhelm the Barcelona midfield with their physicality and aggression.

Therefore, it will be interesting to see who Flick picks as the desired replacement for Rodri in the centre of the park this evening.

articles.title: Crystal Palace Hopeful Of Huge Result Against Liverpool
articles.summary: Crystal Palace host Liverpool in huge Premier League clash.
articles.body:
Henry Swain previews Palace's clash with Liverpool.

Crystal Palace host Andoni Iraola's Liverpool side in a huge Premier League clash at Selhurst Park. Palace will be looking to finally produce a positive performance, and if they fail to do so it could be costly for Pierre Sage in terms of his future at the club.

Palace come into the game off the back of a disappointing performance in midweek, which was saved by a late Daichi Kamada equaliser. Liverpool will also be looking to bounce back after a difficult away trip to Istanbul, where they were beaten by Fenerbahçe 3-2.

Liverpool will be looking to close the gap on those sides at the top of the table, and a win could put them into the top four depending on results elsewhere on Sunday afternoon.

For Palace , full focus has to be on somehow finding a result to kickstart the season. Nottingham Forest found that exact performance against Manchester City on Saturday evening, and it feels as if Palace are almost desperate for a similar performance and result at home to one of the division's top sides.

In the last ten games in all competitions, Palace actually edge out on top very slightly. Four wins betters Liverpool's three, with three also ending level.

Until last season's trip to Anfield, Palace were unbeaten against the Reds in the previous four games, which included the Community Shield final of course. Last season, including that penalty shootout win, Palace beat Liverpool three times.

A 3-1 win at Anfield in the Carabao Cup came after Palace had beaten the Reds at Selhurst Park courtesy of a last minute Eddie Nketiah strike.

There have been a number of memorable encounters between the two sides, but overall, Liverpool do completely dominate the fixture. In games at Selhurst Park in the Premier League, Liverpool have won eleven, with Palace coming out victorious on just three occasions.

Ismaïla Sarr has been a key figure for Palace against Liverpool in recent seasons, but Pierre Sage will be without the forward who remains injured until after the international break.

Aside from a narrow 1-0 victory over Fulham in the Carabao Cup, Palace have not won a game in the last seven, which has seen the pressure pile high on the shoulders of manager Pierre Sage, who could face the sack if another bad performance is produced in this game.

The biggest issue as of late has been the manner of the defeats, not necessarily the scorelines themselves. Palace are playing without a clear identity, and there have been multiple games where they've simply not looked like a Premier League side.

With the international break beginning just after this game, it would be a good time to bring a new man in if that is the plan. It's unlikely that many of Palace's players will be selected for their international sides considering the levels of performance that they have been producing this season, which would give a manager time on the training pitch with them.

The issue is, is that time is something that was never afforded to Sage himself, so if the club choose to stick, it could well be that a couple of weeks on the grass is exactly what Palace need.

Expecting a win against Liverpool is unrealistic, but the bare minimum expectation will be a gutsy performance, where Palace at the very least compete with their opponents.

If they can do that, Sage may just earn himself some more time, and the opportunity to take on both Hull City and Coventry following the break.

articles.title: Barcelona new signing has a point to prove against Atletico Madrid after poor precedent
articles.summary: Barcelona travel to the Metropolitano this weekend for one of the most important matches of the season.It promises to be an important game for many of the Ba...
articles.body:
Barcelona travel to the Metropolitano this weekend for one of the most important matches of the season.

It promises to be an important game for many of the Barcelona players, including the new signing Anthony Gordon, who will play his first competitive game at the Metropolitano.

Barcelona's poor record against Atleti last season has already been well-documented , but this particular game is even more important for Gordon, who has had a bad precedent as well.

Can Gordon make an impact against Atletico Madrid? (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

As reported by Diario SPORT , Gordon has faced Atletico Madrid only once in his career. It was in August last year in the Sepa Cup, and it wasn't the best of experiences for the winger.

Deployed through the middle as Newcastle United slipped to a 2-0 defeat, it was a bruising afternoon for Gordon.

The Englishman found fierce resistance from the Atleti defence and was eventually forced off in the 85th minute due to ankle discomfort.

This could be an early reminder that Diego Simeone's men could employ the same method when it comes to putting a halt to Gordon in the final third.

This time, however, the Barcelona player will operate from the flanks, which should give the Englishman a higher degree of freedom.

Godon needs to up his performances once again. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

With three goals and five assists in all competitions, it will be perhaps unfair to criticise Gordon's performances since joining Barcelona in the summer.

The winger has won his battle with Karim Adeyemi for the left wing role, and established himself as a first-team regular.

Yet, question marks remain. Gordon notably endured a poor outing against Real Madrid in the season's first El Clasico and is still yet to score his first away goal in La Liga.

His only goals in La Liga so far have come at home against Getafe and Alaves. That is quite a modest tally for a player of his quality.

A strong performance against Atletico Madrid, to that end, could serve as an ideal confidence-booster for the former Newcastle United starlet, as he looks to solidify his role in Flick's setup.

articles.title: Un corazón dividido en dos: una mitad txuriurdin y otra rayista
articles.standfirst: Ambos equipos han compartido varios protagonistas muy queridos por la afición. "Es especial", afirmó Beñat en la previa
articles.summary: Ambos equipos han compartido varios protagonistas muy queridos por la afición. "Es especial", afirmó Beñat en la previa
articles.body: San José vuelve a casa. Después de dirigir en tres continentes y de visitar Anoeta para enfrentarse contra el Sanse con el Eibar (obtuvo una victoria por 0-1), el guipuzcoano se medirá con su Rayo al primer equipo txuriurdin por primera vez. Atrás se quedaron esos años como entrenador de los 'potrillos' en los campos de Zubieta. Ahora, con una franja en el pecho, el entrenador buscará la victoria ante un equipo que viene de empatar a uno contra el Olympique de Lyon. Beñat comenzó en los banquillos del Antiguoko en el barrio de El Antiguo en San Sebastián. Un club con mucha representación en la élite futbolística como Martín Zubimendi, Ander Barrenetxea o Unai López. Por sus filas han pasado exjugadores que hoy son grandes entrenadores como Xabi Alonso, Andoni Iraola o Mikel Arteta. La élite inglesa. En este club, el actual técnico del Rayo Vallecano dio sus primeros pasos en los banquillos, antes de mudarse a Zubieta. En la cantera realista pasó varias temporadas y acabó siendo entrenador del cadete. Una llamada de Raúl Caneda, para que se hiciera cargo del filial de Al Ittihad frenó su progresión en Zubieta y se marchó al extranjero, donde cosechó la mayoría de sus éxitos. Aún así, Beñat no olvida sus orígenes. "Es especial. Es mi casa, es mi ciudad, donde nací futbolísticamente y como entrenador. Conozco a casi todo el mundo. El equipo de toda mi vida. Es muy emocional", comenzó en la rueda de prensa. Aunque será una vuelta a casa emocionante, Beñat San José lo tiene claro. "Hemos analizado a un grandísimo equipo que conozco muy bien y vamos a ir con todo para conseguir los tres puntos". Ayudará que el Rayo Vallecano lleve tiempo haciéndose 'experto' en Anoeta. En las dos últimas campañas ha conseguido la victoria. La temporada pasada, con un gol del Pacha Espino en los minutos finales del encuentro. Además de Beñat San José, ambas entidades han compartido varios jugadores de los que se tiene gran recuerdo en el feudo rayista. Julen Lopetegui fue el portero del primer Euro Rayo y canterano de la Real; Raúl Tamudo fue jugador txuriurdin antes de erigirse como héroe en Vallecas y Labaka eligió el barrio para retirarse del fútbol, después de estar una vida ligado a la Real. El último enfrentamiento entre ambos equipos estuvo marcado por la polémica arbitral. El resultado fue un 3-3 en Vallecas y la entidad rayista protestó varias acciones en su contra. La primera, un gol anulado a Ratiu por una mano en uno de los controles previos, y la segunda, cuando José Luis Guzmán anuló un gol a Pedro Díaz para pitar un penalti a favor de la Real. Se tuvo que vestir de héroe Alemao para empatar el encuentro. El Rayo volverá a visitar el frío norte con un objetivo entre ceja y ceja: la victoria. Los tres puntos acercarían al cuadro franjirrojo a los puestos europeos antes del parón de selecciones. A por el tres de tres.

articles.title: Liverpool look to Premier League rivals for Alisson replacement
articles.summary: Liverpool Weigh Bart Verbruggen Move as Brighton Goalkeeper Emerges on Transfer RadarLiverpool are assessing the goalkeeper market ahead of a potentially imp...
articles.body:
Liverpool Weigh Bart Verbruggen Move as Brighton Goalkeeper Emerges on Transfer Radar

Liverpool are assessing the goalkeeper market ahead of a potentially important summer, with Bart Verbruggen among the names under consideration as planning continues around the future of Alisson Becker.

According to Caught Offside , the Brighton goalkeeper is attracting close attention after a strong campaign in which he has continued to enhance a growing reputation in the Premier League. The Dutch international, still only 24, is viewed by a number of leading clubs as a high-upside option with both top-flight pedigree and significant room for further development.

Liverpool's interest appears to fit a broader piece of succession planning. Verbruggen has produced impressive numbers this season, recording 11 clean sheets in 14 appearances across all competitions, and that output has helped place him firmly on the radar of clubs operating at the top end of the market.

The sense around this situation is that Liverpool have tracked him for some time rather than reacting only to a short burst of form. That is often how recruitment decisions of this scale are shaped, with long-term monitoring, character checks and tactical suitability all carrying weight before any formal move is explored.

What sharpens the issue is uncertainty around Alisson. The report states Liverpool are preparing for the possibility of the Brazilian leaving next summer, which naturally places greater urgency on identifying credible alternatives. When a first-choice goalkeeper enters a delicate contract position, clubs rarely leave succession work until late in the process.

Verbruggen's profile is appealing for obvious reasons. He has experience in England, he is young enough to grow into the role, and he has shown composure at a club where goalkeepers are regularly asked to contribute in and out of possession.

Brighton goalkeeper faces elite competition

Any deal would be far from straightforward. Manchester United, Chelsea, Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are all said to be monitoring Verbruggen, underlining the level of regard for him across Europe. Liverpool may therefore need to move decisively if their interest develops into something more concrete.

At this stage, there is no suggestion of an advanced move, but the logic is easy to follow. If Liverpool are preparing for change in goal, Verbruggen looks like one of the more credible long-term options available.

This is exactly the sort of report that grabs attention because it makes sense on several levels. Verbruggen has looked assured, modern and unfazed by the pace of Premier League football. For a club thinking beyond the immediate term, he feels like a sensible name to keep high on the list.

The biggest question is whether this is genuine succession planning or simply good market awareness. Liverpool should always know who the best young goalkeepers are, especially if there is any uncertainty around a senior figure. That does not automatically mean a transfer is close, but it does suggest serious preparation behind the scenes.

There is also the Brighton factor. They are tough sellers, they know player value, and they rarely allow top talent to leave cheaply. If several heavyweight clubs are in the same conversation, the price would quickly become significant. Liverpool would need to be certain that Verbruggen is the right successor rather than one of several good options.

What stands out most is the age profile. At 24, he could arrive and own the position for years. That matters. Replacing a goalkeeper of Alisson's stature is not about finding someone merely good enough for one season, it is about identifying the next cornerstone. Verbruggen has the look of someone who could grow into that responsibility, and that is what makes this link feel worth watching.

articles.title: Football match remembers WW1 Christmas truce
articles.summary: Newark Town plays a side from its German twin town of Emmendingen to remember the 1914 truce.
articles.body:
A football match commemorating the World War One Christmas truce has taken place in Nottinghamshire.

On Christmas Day 1914, British and German troops stopped fighting and met at several locations in Belgium. A soldier from Newark, William Setchfield, was present at one near the village of Messines and he may have provided the football used during the truce.

On Saturday, Newark Town played a side from its twin town of Emmendingen in what was billed a Peace Match.

Luke Parsons, manager of Newark Town FC, said: "We've played previously. It's two histories, two cultures coming together to symbolise the friendship of what we are about."

He added: "Obviously that was put down 108 years ago and we want to continue that with this game."

The two teams have played each other twice before at the site of the front lines in Belgium for the centenary of the event.

However, this was the first time Emmendingen FC had come to Newark to play.

Parsons said: "It makes me incredibly proud to invite them over to England to fulfill another fixture."

Jakob Griessbaum, captain of Emmendingen FC, said the team was "honoured" to visit and play in the match.

"It's a nice opportunity for us to get together," he added.

"We are happy to play football, to think about World War One and what happened there."

Francis Towndrow, local historian for Newark Town FC, who was at the game, said the score in the two previous encounters was 4-1 to the German team, and then 2-2, but Newark won on penalties.

"The Germans have been itching to play again to beat us so it's wonderful they are here," he added.

The final score of the game, played at the YMCA centre in Lord Hawke Way on Saturday, was a 2-0 win to Newark.

The Blues thanked Emmendingen and wished them "safe travels home", adding: "Thank you to all that came out to support.

"Football is the winner. Fantastic to be a part of."

Towndrow said research had revealed accounts of how good Setchfield was as a goalkeeper.

He added: "We can from that deduce that he may have played in goal that day and also that [the] football he got for Christmas was used."

Towndrow said Setchfield survived the war and stayed in the Nottinghamshire area. He died in 1959 at the age of 71.

articles.title: 📸 This league ended in heartbreak last night 🫢
articles.summary: This one's brutal.It's the scene going around the world this morning: a huge misunderstanding and a crushing reality check in Argentine football.It all happe...
articles.body:
It's the scene going around the world this morning: a huge misunderstanding and a crushing reality check in Argentine football.

It all happened on the final day of the Liga Profesional season.

As the final whistle blew at their home ground, Rosario Central supporters invaded the pitch in wild celebration.

Flares lit, tears of joy, hugs with the players: the whole stadium was already celebrating the Argentine league title, convinced that rivals Boca Juniors had failed to beat Defensa y Justicia.

But hundreds of kilometres away, with La Bombonera holding its breath, everything changed in the 96th minute.

That was the precise moment Enner Valencia popped up to score the winner (1-0), confirmed by VAR after an agonising wait.

On the pitch at Rosario, Angel Di Maria's club, the party stopped dead.

Phones began to buzz, the false news was dispelled, and the incredible collective euphoria gave way to utter despair, stunned faces and motionless supporters with their heads in their hands.

articles.title: Lionel Messi scripts MLS history! Inter Miami superstar becomes first player to win back-to-back Golden Boots
articles.summary: Lionel Messi continues to rewrite the record books in Major League Soccer, with the Inter Miami captain becoming the first player in the league's history
articles.body: Lionel Messi continues to rewrite the record books in Major League Soccer, with the Inter Miami captain becoming the first player in the league's history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. At 39, the Argentine superstar showed no signs of slowing down, finishing the 2026 regular season with 26 goals to claim the scoring title for the second year running.Messi finished four goals ahead of FC Dallas forward Petar Musa, who managed 22, while Vancouver Whitecaps FC's Brian White occupied third place with 20 goals. The latest honour also made Messi only the sixth player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot multiple times.Messi's incredible scoring numbers power Inter Miami captain to another Golden BootIn his fourth MLS season, Messi topped the scoring charts despite featuring in just 31 regular-season matches. His 26 goals were accompanied by 17 assists, taking his overall goal contributions to 43 — the third-highest tally recorded in a single MLS season.The Argentine also led the league in goals per game, averaging 0.87, and shared the top spot for the most multi-goal performances with six. He ranked second in goals per 90 minutes, with an impressive average of 0.91.One of the standout aspects of Messi's campaign was his productivity from open play. Of his 26 goals, only one came from the penalty spot, leaving him with 25 non-penalty goals — the second-highest single-season tally in MLS history. The record belongs to Messi himself, who scored 28 non-penalty goals in 2025.Back-to-back 25-goal seasons put Messi in elite MLS companyMessi's latest Golden Boot further extended his remarkable consistency in front of goal. After scoring 29 times in the 2025 regular season, he became only the second player in MLS history to register at least 25 goals in consecutive campaigns.His dominance has been equally impressive over a longer period. Messi has scored 75 regular-season goals across the last three campaigns, the second-highest tally by any player in a three-season period in MLS history.He is also only the second player, alongside 2023 Golden Boot winner Denis Bouanga, to score at least 20 goals in three consecutive regular seasons.Messi's 43 goal contributions create another MLS milestoneWhile his goals have grabbed the headlines, Messi's creative influence has been equally significant. His 43 goal contributions in 2026 made him the first player in MLS history to register at least 40 goal contributions in successive seasons.His numbers across the 2024-2026 period underline the scale of his impact. Messi has accumulated 127 goal contributions during these three seasons, comprising goals and assists. That is 28 more than the next-best tally of 98, recorded by Evander over the same period.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
